method: Read-only source and Git review; target repository code and tests were not executed.
caveats: The 200-commit limit selects non-merge commits before fix/bug/regression subject filtering; it is not 200 fixes per repository.
source_files counts eligible tracked paths; function_bodies counts extracted named function bodies before the 45-1200-token candidate index filter.
HEAD parse errors are recorded per file; unaffected parsed bodies in those files may still be included. Historical parse errors are not separately counted.
All repositories are shallow clones. No selected fix commit lacked its parent, but this does not cover older history.
The detector excludes test/example/generated/vendor paths, requires matching file extensions, and does not expand Rust macros.
The pnpm checkout includes extensive Rust and TypeScript source, so repository primary-language groups are not language-isolated samples.
One emitted candidate is too little to establish general precision. No independently labelled recall set was built; rejected samples do not estimate recall.
Exact whole-function matching intentionally misses partial clones and legitimate signature or body differences; same-spelled external types and members are not resolved.

rejected_example.reason: The constructor addition stores distPath for a new child-process watchdog. ThreadsPoolWorker uses node:worker_threads, a different entrypoint, and thread.terminate(); the fork PID watchdog does not transfer to this worker backend.

evidence.fact: Stores distPath; start uses it in watchProcess(this._fork, this.distPath) at line 72.
Entrypoint literal is workers/threads.js, unlike workers/forks.js; this whole-body difference is enough for exact rejection.
Constructs node:worker_threads Worker; stop calls thread.terminate at line 65.
watchProcess requires ChildProcess and tracks child.pid.
On parent IPC disconnect the watchdog kills tracked process IDs with SIGKILL.

rejected_example.confidence: Source-supported avoided false positive; no target runtime execution.
